hypothesis: The two valid prior OpenMP variants measured nearly the same aggregate time (0.241145 and 0.241645 seconds) against the 0.464905-second serial baseline, and the supplied outcomes do not separate one- from four-thread timings. This candidate tests a different cost: it keeps one team across all six timesteps but assigns contiguous row chunks once, replacing repeated worksharing dispatch with an explicit barrier after each step. Less dispatch overhead could help; the barriers or imbalance could offset it. Correctness and native timings, including initialization, remain for controller evaluation.
notes: This is a distinct persistent-team implementation: each worker receives a deterministic contiguous chunk of interior z/y rows, and an explicit barrier completes each timestep before the next reads its inputs. The thread request is positive-clamped and capped by the available row count. Initialization and the original update bounds and buffer parity are preserved. No target-specific compiler or hardware facts were supplied, and no source edit was compiled or measured here.
transformations: Replace the serial six-step sweep with one persistent OpenMP team requesting no more than the positive threads budget and available row count.
Partition interior z/y rows deterministically into contiguous per-thread chunks instead of using repeated OpenMP worksharing loops.
Use an explicit barrier after each timestep so all output rows are complete before the next timestep reads them.
Preserve full buffer initialization, six-step even/odd buffer parity, stencil expression, and interior update bounds.
